content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am working on an industrial washing machine control project using a variable frequency drive for agitation. I am struggling to transfer the program from my computer to the [product_name]. My configuration is as follows: [product_name] IP Address: 192.168.1.17, Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0, Gateway: 192.168.1.254. The computer's IP is 192.168.1.20, whether static or dynamic, directly connected to a switch. The LAN cable functions perfectly; I've tested it. I consistently receive a timeout error. It's particularly frustrating because sometimes the transfer works without explanation, but most attempts fail and I can't transfer the program. I've attached the program to illustrate the full issue. There is LAN connectivity as I can start/stop the [product_name] and set the time, but downloading any program doesn't work, regardless of complexity. I welcome your feedback.

Please avoid posting the same issue in multiple threads. You've described your problem in another topic as well (see post #12): Cannot transfer program due to timeout between PC and [product_name]. Your program can be uploaded to my [product_name] without any problems, as I've shown in the other thread. Why did you enter a gateway address? Are the [product_name] and PC in different subnets? Have you selected the correct network adapter in the transmission window? Is the IP address for the [product_name] being used elsewhere?

Apologies, I am new to this platform and wasn’t sure if my earlier message was posted, so I tried to delete it. I have correctly selected the adapter; I'm using a USB LAN adapter. After some time, I get a timeout error or it says the program has been loaded, but checking the [product_name] shows it is empty. I am not sure what to try next. I attempted loading from the SD card, but it reports that no program is present. Thanks for your help.

How are we supposed to assist you remotely without seeing all settings and details? What is the IP address of your USB/LAN adapter? Please provide the exact IP and subnet mask. I suspect an IP address issue may be causing this. Are you also trying to load the program via SD card? In that case, you must save the program as a .bin file with a specific name on your computer and then copy it to the SD card. Make sure the SD card is formatted with FAT32, and its capacity should not exceed 32 GB.
The [product_name] should have a fixed IP address. Did you manually set its IP?

I’ve taken a screenshot. Whether I assign an IP automatically or manually, neither option solves the issue. I am using a 64 GB SD card, so perhaps the card size is causing problems with visibility for the [product_name].
Yes, the [product_name] has a fixed IP of 192.168.1.17 and subnet mask 255.255.255.0, with no gateway assigned.
You need to create a FAT32 partition on the SD card with a maximum size of 32 GB.

Thank you for your support. After formatting the SD card as advised, the program was successfully read. I’m still unsure why the IP connection works intermittently, but it is less important now since I can proceed with my test and training PLC. I’ll investigate IP address configuration further. Thanks again.

Hello, disconnect the [product_name] from your network and ping its IP address. There might be an IP conflict. Could you provide the order number of your [product_name] and the version number of [product_name] software you are using? You might need a software update. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering inconsistent issues when transferring programs from a PC to [product_name] over LAN. While network controls like starting and stopping the [product_name] and adjusting time settings work, the actual program download frequently results in a timeout, often for unclear reasons. Transfer via SD card initially failed due to improper formatting and exceeded size limits, underlining the importance of clear instructions on card type and size requirements.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a reliable and consistent process for program transfer from PC to [product_name] over LAN. They wish to receive clearer guidance or meaningful error messages regarding both network configuration and SD card requirements to avoid failed transfers.
